title: Pathogenesis and natural history of Machupo virus infection in nonhuman primates.
abstract: UNLABELLED: The mammarenavirus Machupo virus (MACV) is the causative agent of Bolivian hemorrhagic fever (BHF) and is associated with high mortality rates in humans and nonhuman primates (NHPs). There are currently no approved vaccines or treatments to combat BHF. As there are eight genetically distinct lineages of MACV, medical countermeasures are needed to protect against all strains within these lineages. While rodent models have been developed for a few strains of MACV, NHPs most faithfully reproduce human disease. However, NHP models have only been described for two strains of MACV. Here, we assessed the pathogenic potential of two genetically distinct strains of MACV representing two different lineages in cynomolgus and/or African green monkeys (AGM). Both MACV strains caused severe multisystemic disease consistent with BHF, often resulting in fatality with the lineage III strain resulting in uniform lethality in both NHP species and the lineage VIII strain resulting in uniform lethality in AGM. Pathology was consistent among the MACV strains and NHP species with primary involvement of the gastrointestinal and lymphoid systems with the central nervous system showing variable but widespread dissemination of MACV antigen. Spatial proteomics showed that MACV antigen was most prevalent in neurons (MAP2+) and Purkinje cells (MAP2+/Calbindin+). Multi-omics assessment of circulating mRNA and proteins showed the overall phenotype of BHF was similar between species; however, the magnitude of the inflammatory response diverged at late timepoints. Overall, MACV infection of NHP recapitulated BHF in humans driven by a dysregulated innate response resulting in vascular inflammation and hemodynamic instability. IMPORTANCE: Machupo virus (MACV) is a deadly and understudied mammarenavirus that causes severe disease known as Bolivian hemorrhagic fever (BHF) with high mortality rates in symptomatic humans. MACV is transmitted to humans by contact with the vesper mouse and has significant outbreak potential. No licensed vaccine or antivirals against MACV exist. Well-characterized animal models are critically needed to test the efficacy of promising candidate medical countermeasures against MACV and to understand how MACV causes disease. Here, we developed several new nonhuman primate models that accurately reproduced human BHF. We utilized spatial proteomics to reveal specific cell types involved in MACV infection, including those within the central nervous system, and employed a multi-omics approach to reveal circulating mRNA and protein biomarkers driving fatal disease outcomes. Our comprehensive investigation of the response to MACV infection in a highly translational species can be exploited to develop new countermeasures to combat BHF.

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究为 NHP 中的 发病机制 和 Machupo 病毒感染的自然史提供了新的见解,证明了这些模型在测试 BHF 医疗对策方面的实用性。研究结果揭示了参与感染的特定细胞类型和导致致命结果的循环生物标志物。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为制定对抗 BHF 的新对策提供信息,并加深对马丘波病毒如何致病的了解。NHP 模型准确地再现了人类 BHF,为医疗对策测试提供了宝贵的工具。

title: Evaluation of Lassa fever surveillance system in Edo State, Nigeria (2024–2025)
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Lassa fever is a priority disease in Nigeria. Periodic evaluation of its surveillance systems is essential to strengthen performance and ensure efficient use of limited public health resources. This study evaluated the Lassa fever surveillance system in Edo State, Nigeria. METHODS: The evaluation followed the 2001 CDC guidelines and used a cross-sectional mixed-methods design. We reviewed statewide surveillance data from 2024-2025 and selected respondents from 26 health facilities across 15 of the 18 (83.3%) local government areas (LGAs), as well as from the state surveillance unit and WHO. We assessed the surveillance system's evolution, structure, and resource availability. We analyzed surveillance data by person, place, and time and audited the data for completeness, errors, outliers, and timeliness. Case investigation forms, laboratory forms, and line lists were reviewed to assess variable usefulness and identify data gaps. Structured questionnaires were administered to 30 stakeholders, including 11 key informant interviews, to assess the system's usefulness, simplicity, acceptability, timeliness, and representativeness. Quantitative data were analyzed descriptively, while qualitative data were analyzed thematically. RESULTS: Since 1969, the Lassa fever surveillance system has evolved from sporadic paper-based reporting to a coordinated, case-based digital platform. Structurally, the system operates from the community to the national level and relies on human resources, surveillance tools, and physical and digital infrastructure. Between 2024 and 2025, 6,296 suspected Lassa fever cases were reported, of which 461 (7.3%) were confirmed, among which 69 (15.0%) died. Three LGAs, Etsako West (204; 44.3%), Esan West (95; 20.6%), and Esan North-East (79; 17.1%), accounted for 378 (82%) confirmed cases. Cases occurred year-round, with increased frequency between November and April. Data completeness exceeded 95%, while errors and outliers were both below 5%. Timeliness assessment indicated that 88.5% of laboratory results were returned within 48 hours and 91.2% of cases were notified within three days. However, 18.7% of cases presented to facilities later than one week after symptom onset. Overall, the system demonstrated strong performance across the assessed attributes. Key operational challenges included delayed or incomplete laboratory feedback, high clinician workload, reliance on Disease Surveillance and Notification Officers to complete forms, and defective electronic devices. Identified data gaps included an unclear definition of the variable "department," incomplete documentation of "date of death" and "department," and the absence of a "cause of death" variable. CONCLUSION: The Lassa fever surveillance system in Edo State is simple, acceptable, and effective for case detection and outbreak monitoring. Addressing identified operational and data quality gaps could further strengthen system efficiency, sustainability, and public health impact.

title_zh: 尼日利亚埃多州拉沙热 监测系统评估(2024-2025年)
source_body_en: INTRODUCTION: Lassa fever is a priority disease in Nigeria. Periodic evaluation of its surveillance systems is essential to strengthen performance and ensure efficient use of limited public health resources. This study evaluated the Lassa fever surveillance system in Edo State, Nigeria. METHODS: The evaluation followed the 2001 CDC guidelines and used a cross-sectional mixed-methods design. We reviewed statewide surveillance data from 2024-2025 and selected respondents from 26 health facilities across 15 of the 18 (83.3%) local government areas (LGAs), as well as from the state surveillance unit and WHO. We assessed the surveillance system's evolution, structure, and resource availability. We analyzed surveillance data by person, place, and time and audited the data for completeness, errors, outliers, and timeliness. Case investigation forms, laboratory forms, and line lists were reviewed to assess variable usefulness and identify data gaps. Structured questionnaires were administered to 30 stakeholders, including 11 key informant interviews, to assess the system's usefulness, simplicity, acceptability, timeliness, and representativeness. Quantitative data were analyzed descriptively, while qualitative data were analyzed thematically. RESULTS: Since 1969, the Lassa fever surveillance system has evolved from sporadic paper-based reporting to a coordinated, case-based digital platform. Structurally, the system operates from the community to the national level and relies on human resources, surveillance tools, and physical and digital infrastructure. Between 2024 and 2025, 6,296 suspected Lassa fever cases were reported, of which 461 (7.3%) were confirmed, among which 69 (15.0%) died. Three LGAs, Etsako West (204; 44.3%), Esan West (95; 20.6%), and Esan North-East (79; 17.1%), accounted for 378 (82%) confirmed cases. Cases occurred year-round, with increased frequency between November and April. Data completeness exceeded 95%, while errors and outliers were both below 5%. Timeliness assessment indicated that 88.5% of laboratory results were returned within 48 hours and 91.2% of cases were notified within three days. However, 18.7% of cases presented to facilities later than one week after symptom onset. Overall, the system demonstrated strong performance across the assessed attributes. Key operational challenges included delayed or incomplete laboratory feedback, high clinician workload, reliance on Disease Surveillance and Notification Officers to complete forms, and defective electronic devices. Identified data gaps included an unclear definition of the variable "department," incomplete documentation of "date of death" and "department," and the absence of a "cause of death" variable. CONCLUSION: The Lassa fever surveillance system in Edo State is simple, acceptable, and effective for case detection and outbreak monitoring. Addressing identified operational and data quality gaps could further strengthen system efficiency, sustainability, and public health impact.

title: Epidemiological profile and outcomes of suspected viral haemorrhagic fever and confirmed Lassa fever admissions in Adamawa State, Nigeria, 2020–2026
abstract: Introduction: Nigeria reports the largest number of Lassa fever cases worldwide, but facility-level data from Adamawa State, north-eastern Nigeria, are lacking. This study describes suspected viral haemorrhagic fever (VHF) admissions, including laboratory-confirmed Lassa fever, at Modibbo Adama University Teaching Hospital, Yola (MAUTHY). Methods: We reviewed the MAUTHY isolation ward register (May 2020–April 2026) for admissions with VHF or Lassa fever recorded as a working or differential diagnosis. Case fatality was calculated among patients with known final vital status. Fisher’s exact tests, Wilson 95% confidence intervals (CIs) and Firth penalised logistic regression were used. Results: Of 330 admissions, 53 (16.1%) were for suspected VHF. Of 40 (75.5%) with a recorded laboratory result, 9 (22.5%) were confirmed Lassa fever. Median age was 28 years; 27 (50.9%) were male. Annual admissions were 1, 3, 12, 11, 13 and 5 in 2020–2025 and 7 in January–April 2026; 34 of 52 dated admissions (65.4%) occurred in January–April. Of 41 patients with known vital status, 15 died (case fatality 36.6%; 95% CI 23.6–51.9); 12 were transferred or had no recorded outcome. Case fatality varied between years (p=0.043) without a linear trend. Age and sex were not associated with death (30–44 vs 15–29 years: adjusted odds ratio 1.88; 95% CI 0.48–7.72). Conclusion: Suspected VHF was a frequent cause of isolation admission, with high in-hospital mortality, year-to-year variation peaking in 2024 and dry-season clustering. Few patients were laboratory-confirmed, so these findings describe suspected VHF rather than confirmed Lassa fever. Faster Lassa virus testing and complete recording of test results and outcomes are priorities.

title: An ESCRT-engineered mRNA-VLP vaccine elicits humoral and cellular immunity against Lassa virus.
abstract: Lassa virus (LASV) causes severe hemorrhagic fever across West Africa, yet no licensed vaccine is available. A major barrier to LASV antigen design is that its sole neutralization target, the glycoprotein complex (GPC), lacks intrinsic late-domain motifs required to engage the host ESCRT machinery for particle release. Here, we report a rational design strategy that confers autonomous budding capacity to LASV GPC by appending a synthetic ESCRT-recruitment cassette to its cytoplasmic domain. Systematic screening of a sixteen-construct matrix identified a lead candidate, VLPdEm5. This construct integrates the ESCRT cassette, an optimized furin cleavage site, and a heterologous H1N1 transmembrane-cytoplasmic domain to support efficient particle assembly and proper display of conformational neutralizing epitopes. Delivered via lipid-nanoparticle-encapsulated mRNA (mRNA-LNP), VLPdEm5 drives efficient in situ virus-like particle (VLP) self-assembly, eliciting rapid, high-titer binding antibodies with broad cross-reactivity across six major LASV lineages, robust germinal center B-cell activity, and memory T-cell responses. Crucially, VLPdEm5 mRNA-LNP provides dose-dependent protection against pseudovirus challenge in vivo. This work establishes an effective LASV vaccine candidate and validates an ESCRT-engineered mRNA-VLP platform broadly applicable to non-budding viral envelope proteins.

title_zh: ESCRT 工程改造的 mRNA-VLP 疫苗 可引发针对拉沙病毒的体液和细胞免疫。
source_body_en: Lassa virus (LASV) causes severe hemorrhagic fever across West Africa, yet no licensed vaccine is available. A major barrier to LASV antigen design is that its sole neutralization target, the glycoprotein complex (GPC), lacks intrinsic late-domain motifs required to engage the host ESCRT machinery for particle release. Here, we report a rational design strategy that confers autonomous budding capacity to LASV GPC by appending a synthetic ESCRT-recruitment cassette to its cytoplasmic domain. Systematic screening of a sixteen-construct matrix identified a lead candidate, VLPdEm5. This construct integrates the ESCRT cassette, an optimized furin cleavage site, and a heterologous H1N1 transmembrane-cytoplasmic domain to support efficient particle assembly and proper display of conformational neutralizing epitopes. Delivered via lipid-nanoparticle-encapsulated mRNA (mRNA-LNP), VLPdEm5 drives efficient in situ virus-like particle (VLP) self-assembly, eliciting rapid, high-titer binding antibodies with broad cross-reactivity across six major LASV lineages, robust germinal center B-cell activity, and memory T-cell responses. Crucially, VLPdEm5 mRNA-LNP provides dose-dependent protection against pseudovirus challenge in vivo. This work establishes an effective LASV vaccine candidate and validates an ESCRT-engineered mRNA-VLP platform broadly applicable to non-budding viral envelope proteins.

title: Public health response to the first reported human case of lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus infection in the United Kingdom since the 1950s
abstract: Abstract The rodent-borne lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) was identified by metagenomic sequencing of cerebrospinal fluid from an immunocompromised 60-year-old individual. The household had recently had a rodent infestation and though environmental home sampling was negative for LCMV, this was assessed as the most likely source. Our investigations suggested the risk to others was low. Increasing availability of clinical metagenomics may help identify more cases in the future. We recommend a proportionate public health response, focusing on those vulnerable to severe disease.

title: A Mathematical Model of Dengue and Lassa Fever Co-Infection with Education and Vector Control
abstract: Dengue and Lassa fever co-circulate in Nigeria, yet few models examine their co-infection alongside behavioural and clinical interventions. This study develops a deterministic compartmental model of dengue–Lassa fever co-infection that couples human, mosquito and rodent dynamics and distinguishes educated from uneducated susceptible individuals. We derive the basic and effective reproduction numbers using the next-generation operator approach, and establish local and global stability of the disease-free equilibrium via a Lyapunov function, together with global stability of the endemic equilibria using a Goh–Volterra function. Sensitivity analysis identifies the parameters that most strongly influence transmission, and the model is calibrated against Nigerian surveillance data. Numerical simulations confirm the analytical results and show that public education, reduced human–vector contact and treatment of co-infected cases lower infection levels.

title: Community Engagement and Involvement in Lassa Fever Control: Implementation, Governance, and Community Outcomes in Selected Districts in Sierra Leone
abstract: This study examined the factors influencing the effectiveness of institutional and community support systems, focusing on guidance and counselling services in secondary schools and Community Engagement and Involvement (CEI) in Lassa fever control in Sierra Leone. The guidance and counselling component employed a mixed-methods cross-sectional design involving 128 respondents from selected secondary schools in Pujehun District. Data were collected through questionnaires and interviews and analysed using descriptive statistics, multiple linear regression, and qualitative analysis. Findings revealed inadequate counselling infrastructure, weak professional capacity, and substantial barriers, including inadequate materials (74.2%), high pupil–counsellor ratios (71.8%), lack of trained counsellors (69.4%), socioeconomic constraints (68.0%), and limited technology (67.2%). Monitoring and follow-up showed the strongest association with career development (β = 0.165, p = .073), although no individual availability or professional-capacity variable significantly predicted career development (p > .05). The CEI component demonstrated significant differences in the depth and quality of community engagement between Lower Bambara and Njaluahun. Training coverage was higher in Lower Bambara (73.0% vs. 55.4%; χ2 = 4.4, p = .037), while co-production was substantially greater (63.5% vs. 28.6%; χ2 = 17.8, p < .001). Lower Bambara also recorded higher effectiveness (median 13.5 vs. 9.0; p < .001), trust (median 13.0 vs. 11.0; p < .001), surveillance cooperation, and timely case reporting. Qualitative findings highlighted trusted local intermediaries, bidirectional communication, and co-production as important mechanisms. The findings demonstrate that formal availability of services or structures alone does not guarantee effectiveness. Sustainable outcomes require adequately trained personnel, sufficient resources, institutional support, regular and responsive implementation, meaningful participation, and strong local ownership. Strengthening professional capacity, infrastructure, monitoring systems, community co-production, trusted communication, and institutional support is therefore essential for improving both educational counselling and community-based public health interventions in Sierra Leone.

title: Diagnostic yield and positivity trends of RT-PCR testing for suspected Lassa fever in North-Central Nigeria, 2024–2026: a retrospective laboratory-based study
abstract: Abstract Background Lassa fever (LF) is endemic in Nigeria, and RT-PCR is the reference method for confirming suspected cases. Little is known about the diagnostic yield of RT-PCR and recent positivity trends in North-Central Nigeria. This study assessed the diagnostic yield, positivity trends, turnaround time and geographic distribution of RT-PCR results among suspected LF cases and their implications for surveillance efficiency. Methods A retrospective laboratory-based analysis of RT-PCR results was conducted for 782 suspected LF cases tested between 2024 and 2026 at Federal Medical Centre Makurdi, in North-Central Nigeria. Diagnostic yield (proportion of suspected cases testing positive) and positivity rates by year, month and local government area (LGA) were calculated with 95% confidence intervals, and turnaround time from sample collection to testing was summarised as median and interquartile range (IQR). Results Of 782 suspected cases, 103 (13.2%; 95% CI 11.0–15.7) tested positive. Positivity increased from 4.2% in 2024 to 8.9% in 2025 and 16.1% in 2026 (chi-square test for trend, p = 0.002). Positivity was highest in February (30.3%) and lowest in April (2.4%). Median turnaround time was 4 days (IQR 4–8) in 2024, 12 days (IQR 7–43) in 2025 and 2 days (IQR 1–4) in 2026. Makurdi LGA supplied 85.0% of samples (positivity 13.5%); 14 of 21 LGAs recorded no positive cases, most with few samples. Conclusions About one in eight suspected LF cases was RT-PCR positive, with rising positivity from 2024 to 2026, a dry-season peak and shorter turnaround time in 2026. Positivity estimates outside the main testing centre were unstable. Broader sampling, consistently short turnaround times and seasonally informed testing could improve LF surveillance efficiency in the region.

title: Beyond Viral Pathogenesis: Climate Change, Zoonotic Spillover, and the Evolving Epidemiology of Viral Hemorrhagic Fevers
abstract: Viral hemorrhagic fevers (VHFs) represent a major global health threat because they can cause severe systemic illness, hemorrhage, multiorgan dysfunction, and death. Ebola virus, Marburg virus, Lassa virus, and Crimean–Congo hemorrhagic fever virus contribute substantially to the global burden of these diseases. These pathogens employ diverse transmission routes, including vector-borne transmission, zoonotic spillover, and direct exposure to infected bodily fluids. Climate change, land use alterations, urbanization, population growth, and increased human–animal interactions may reshape pathogen ecology and create new opportunities for viral emergence and transmission. International travel and interconnected human populations further complicate outbreak containment. This review examines the pathophysiological mechanisms, epidemiological patterns, and major outbreaks associated with VHFs, with particular emphasis on how environmental change, ecological disruption, and infectious disease dynamics interact. We also evaluate the roles of global health organizations in strengthening disease surveillance, coordinating outbreak responses, and promoting international preparedness. Furthermore, we discuss the importance of integrated surveillance systems, cross-sectoral collaboration, and climate-informed public health strategies in reducing the risks associated with emerging and recurring VHF outbreaks. By integrating virological, ecological, epidemiological, and public health perspectives, this review highlights critical knowledge gaps and identifies priorities for improving early detection, outbreak preparedness, and coordinated responses to future VHF threats.

title: METTL8 orchestrates TFH cell differentiation through m3C-mediated TCF1 regulation in infection and cancer models
abstract: T follicular helper (TFH) cells are critical for humoral immunity against infections and correlate with immunotherapy efficacy, whereas immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy can drive their aberrant expansion, underscoring the need to understand the regulators controlling TFH cell fate. However, the epitranscriptomic regulation of their differentiation remains poorly understood. Here, we identify the 3-methylcytosine (m3C) methyltransferase METTL8 as a key regulator of TFH cell differentiation in both viral infection and cancer. METTL8 was preferentially expressed in CXCL13hi TFH cells, and its deficiency impaired TFH differentiation and germinal center responses in the lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus infection model and following anti-PD-1 immunotherapy in tumor models. Mechanistically, METTL8 exerted dual functions: it bound and stabilized Tcf7 mRNA through m3C modification, and it interacted with TCF1 protein to regulate chromatin accessibility and 3D genome organization at key TFH-associated loci, including Cxcr5 and Il6ra. Notably, ginkgolic acid treatment suppressed TFH responses without compromising the antitumor efficacy of anti-PD-1 therapy, an effect associated with METTL8. Collectively, our findings identify METTL8 as an epitranscriptomic regulator linked to RNA modification, TCF1-associated transcriptional control, and chromatin architecture during TFH differentiation and suggest that modulation of this pathway may provide a strategy to tune TFH-driven immune responses.

title: The transcription factor TOX maintains stemness circuits that sustain longevity and multipotency of progenitor CD4+ T cells in chronic infection.
abstract: Progenitor CD4 + T (Tpex) cells retain developmental plasticity and replenish antigen-specific CD4 + T cell responses in settings of chronic infection and cancer. Given the sustained, elevated expression of the transcription factor TOX across all CD4 + T EX cell subsets during chronic infection, we examined how TOX impacts CD4 + T EX differentiation during chronic infection. Deletion of TOX in lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV)-specific transgenic CD4 + T cells impaired Tpex cell survival and drove unrestrained T EX cell differentiation. Multiomic profiling revealed that this effector-like state was concomitant with loss of TCF-1 pathway activity and gain of NFAT, NF-κB, and RUNX-coordinated transcriptional circuitry. TOX also promoted the multipotent potential of CD4 + Tpex cells to differentiate into T helper (Th)1-like or Tfh-like cells by day 8 post-infection (p.i.) prior to establishment of chronic infection. These data reveal a TOX-driven transcriptional network that maintains CD4 + Tpex cell function and persistence, supporting a durable and malleable response during persisting antigen stimulation.

elements_zh.main_results: 多组学分析表明,TOX 缺失会导致类似效应子的状态,其特征是 TCF-1 通路活性丧失以及 NFAT、NF-κB 和 RUNX 协调的转录回路增加。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,TOX 维持了一个转录网络,支持 CD4+ Tpex 细胞的功能和持久性,从而在长时间抗原暴露期间实现持久且适应性强的反应。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果提供了对慢性感染中维持 CD4+ T 细胞反应的机制的见解,这可以为增强免疫持久性和治疗干预的策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于转基因 CD4+ T 细胞,并未考虑自然感染动态,但由于对 TOX 作用的直接操作和多组学分析,证据是强有力的。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand how the transcription factor TOX influences the maintenance of stemness circuits in progenitor CD4+ T cells during chronic infection, as these cells retain developmental plasticity and replenish antigen-specific responses.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study involved examining the impact of TOX deletion in LCMV-specific transgenic CD4+ T cells during chronic infection, with a focus on their survival and differentiation patterns.
analysis_en.methods: TOX deletion was induced in LCMV-specific transgenic CD4+ T cells, and multiomic profiling was used to analyze changes in transcriptional circuitry associated with effector-like states.
analysis_en.main_results: Multiomic profiling showed that TOX deletion led to an effector-like state characterized by loss of TCF-1 pathway activity and increased NFAT, NF-κB, and RUNX-coordinated transcriptional circuitry.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that TOX maintains a transcriptional network that supports the function and persistence of CD4+ Tpex cells, enabling a durable and adaptable response during prolonged antigen exposure.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide insights into the mechanisms that sustain CD4+ T cell responses in chronic infections, which could inform strategies for enhancing immune persistence and therapeutic interventions.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to transgenic CD4+ T cells and does not account for natural infection dynamics, but the evidence is strong due to the direct manipulation and multiomic analysis of TOX's role.

title_zh: 转录因子 TOX 维持干细胞回路,维持慢性感染中 CD4+ T 祖细胞的寿命和多能性。
source_body_en: Progenitor CD4 + T (Tpex) cells retain developmental plasticity and replenish antigen-specific CD4 + T cell responses in settings of chronic infection and cancer. Given the sustained, elevated expression of the transcription factor TOX across all CD4 + T EX cell subsets during chronic infection, we examined how TOX impacts CD4 + T EX differentiation during chronic infection. Deletion of TOX in lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV)-specific transgenic CD4 + T cells impaired Tpex cell survival and drove unrestrained T EX cell differentiation. Multiomic profiling revealed that this effector-like state was concomitant with loss of TCF-1 pathway activity and gain of NFAT, NF-κB, and RUNX-coordinated transcriptional circuitry. TOX also promoted the multipotent potential of CD4 + Tpex cells to differentiate into T helper (Th)1-like or Tfh-like cells by day 8 post-infection (p.i.) prior to establishment of chronic infection. These data reveal a TOX-driven transcriptional network that maintains CD4 + Tpex cell function and persistence, supporting a durable and malleable response during persisting antigen stimulation.
abstract_zh: CD4 + T 祖细胞 (Tpex) 保留发育可塑性,并在慢性感染和癌症环境中补充抗原特异性 CD4 + T 细胞反应。鉴于慢性感染期间所有 CD4 + T EX 细胞亚群中转录因子 TOX 的表达持续升高,我们研究了 TOX 在慢性感染期间如何影响 CD4 + T EX 分化。淋巴细胞脉络丛脑膜炎病毒 (LCMV) 特异性转基因 CD4 + T 细胞中 TOX 的缺失损害了 Tpex 细胞的存活并驱动了不受限制的 T EX 细胞分化。多组学分析显示,这种效应子样状态伴随着 TCF-1 通路活性的丧失和 NFAT、NF-κB 和 RUNX 协调转录回路的增加。TOX 还促进 CD4 + Tpex 细胞的多能潜能,在感染后 (p.i.) 第 8 天、慢性感染建立之前分化为 T 辅助细胞 (Th)1 样或 Tfh 样细胞。这些数据揭示了 TOX 驱动的转录网络,可维持 CD4 + Tpex 细胞功能和持久性,支持持续抗原刺激期间的持久且可延展的反应。
